full_judgment:
This Rule was issued on an application for revision filed by the plaintiffs under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) against judgment and decree dated 30-7-1987 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Commercial Court, Chittagong in Other Class Appeal No. 582 of 1984 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing judgment and decree dated 6-8-1984 passed by the then learned Munsif, Fatickhari, Chittagong in Other Class Suit No. 2 of 1982 decreeing the suit for permanent injunction instituted in the representative character. 

 6. The trial Court decreed the suit. The contesting defendants appealed against the decree. The lower appellate Court allowed the appeal and dismissed the. suit reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court. 

 7. Feeling aggrieved by impugned judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court, the plaintiffs as the petitioners obtained this Rule from this Court. 

 8. Mr AKM Abdul Hakim, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the lower appellate Court allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court on the ground of maintainability of the suit although the trial Court, assigning reasons, found that the suit as framed was maintainable. He further submits that the lower appellate Court erroneously found that the suit was barred under section 91 of the Local Government Ordinance, 1976, although the contesting defendants did not raise such objection at the initial stage of the suit and, as such, the trial Court found that at the hearing of the suit no such objection was permissible, He lastly submits that the' judgment of lower appellate Court is not a proper judgment as contemplated under Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code. 

 10. I have perused the revisional application and the judgments of the Courts below. The trial Court not only found that the suit was maintainable as framed but it also found that the plaintiffs were successful in making out a case for a decree of permanent injunction against the defendants. The lower appellate Court, on the other hand, found that the suit as framed was not maintainable as the provisions of section 91 of the Local Government Ordinance, 1976 were not complied with prior to the institution of the suit. The fate of this Rule hinges on maintainability of the suit In order to address this point, let us have a glimpse over section 91 of the Local Government Ordinance, 1976. Section 91 runs as follows: 

 12. Section 91 of the Local Government Ordinance, 1976 and section 152 of the Paurashava Ordinance, 1977 were couched in identical language. In the case of Narayanganj Paurashava, represented by its Administrator, Narayanganj; Chairman, Narayanganj Paurashava and others vs Abdur Razzak 46 DLR 295, it has been held that notice under section 152 of the Paurashava Ordinance, 1977 is sine qua non in all circumstances for instituting a suit against the Paurashava for anything done in official capacity. In the above case, the suit was filed against the Paurashava without complying with provisions of section 152 of the Paurashava Ordinance, 1977 and the suit was decreed. The appellate Court affirmed the decree passed in the suit. In such state of affairs, the High Court Division set aside the judgment of both the Courts below for non-compliance with the provisions of section 152 of the Paurashava Ordinance, 1977. Similar view was taken in the case of Zakia Sultana vs Maksuda Parvin and others 8 BLC 168. Therefore, the contention that objection as to maintainability of the suit has to be taken at the earliest opportunity does not stand to reason. Where there are mandatory provisions of law to be complied with before filing a suit, such provisions must be complied with before institution of the suit. In the case ill hand, since the provisions of section 91, Local Government Ordinance, 1976 were not complied with, the suit was not maintainable. As such, the appellate Court correctly found that the case as framed was not maintainable. 

 13. The plaintiffs as the petitioners obtained Rule from this Court impugning judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate Court but on the date of issuance of the Rule, no interim order in the form of injunction was passed against the defendants. Therefore, there was no injunction for the last 18 years. After lapse of 18 years from the date of dismissal of the suit, the plaintiffs now cannot get a decree for permanent injunction.
